expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = | TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription; where each extends SubscriptionBase with status literal

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each interface like TrialingSubscription contains only { status: "trialing"; trialEndsAt: Date; }

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Shows assertNever function with default: return assertNever(sub);

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: type Brand<T, B extends string> = T & { readonly __brand: B }; type SubscriptionId = Brand<string, "SubscriptionId">;

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: type CancelableSubscription = TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription; function cancelSubscription(sub: CancelableSubscription, ...) makes canceled→canceled a type error

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "cancel an already-canceled subscription" is a type error, discusses bag of optionals vs sum type hazard

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Entire response avoids optional-bag interface, uses discriminated union with interfaces.
